_meta.disclaimer: Ramara Hub is an independent community resource. It is not the Township of Ramara's official website. Every answer links to its official source. Always confirm time-sensitive details with the Township at 705-484-5374.

entries.q: Why did my wastewater bill go up 15% in 2026?
entries.a: Council passed Bylaw 2025.76 in December 2025, raising 2026 wastewater rates by 15% instead of the 13% originally planned. The township says wastewater must be fully funded by user rates, not taxes. Mayor Clarke linked the extra increase partly to the cost of trucking effluent from the failing Bayshore Village system. A typical user pays about $217 more in 2026. The full story is in our Wastewater brief.
entries.keywords: sewer bill increase rate hike expensive why cost more

entries.q: What are the 2026 water and wastewater rates?
entries.a: Wastewater (residential): $240.29 fixed per quarter plus $5.00 per cubic metre (Bylaw 2025.76). Water: $160.19 fixed per quarter plus $3.47 per cubic metre (Bylaw 2024.79). Current schedules run to 2033: wastewater planned at about +13% per year, water +8% per year. A comprehensive rate review is due at council in fall 2026.
entries.keywords: price per cubic metre quarterly charge schedule water sewer

entries.q: Who is on municipal water and sewer, and who is on septic?
entries.a: Only Brechin, Lagoon City, and Bayshore Village are on township sewer (two treatment facilities). Seven small municipal water systems serve Brechin/Lagoon City, Park Lane, South Ramara, Bayshore Village, Val Harbour, Davy Drive, and Somerset/Knobhill. Everyone else in Ramara is on private well and septic and does not pay water/wastewater rates — those systems are user-funded by the people connected to them.
entries.keywords: septic well municipal services urban rural who pays connected

entries.q: What is happening with the Bayshore Village wastewater system (WWTF 202)?
entries.a: Bayshore's sprayfields reached end of life, forcing the township to truck effluent away at major cost (a $1.5M loan was needed). In March 2026 council awarded a $24.1M contract to replace the system with tile beds — about $17.6M provincial grant money and $6.5M township. Construction started spring 2026; first tile beds due around November 2026, completion mid-2027.
entries.keywords: bayshore sprayfield tile bed trucking hauling effluent construction

entries.q: Ramara got a $30 million grant — will my rates go down?
entries.a: The province announced $30M for Ramara water/wastewater infrastructure in January 2026, the largest infrastructure grant in township history. The township says the grant does not directly reduce rates — it funds capital projects (mainly the Bayshore rebuild). Council has directed staff to model future rates with and without the grant; that review is expected in fall 2026.
entries.keywords: 30 million provincial funding lower rates relief

entries.q: What did the Lone Birch sewer project end up costing homeowners?
entries.a: The final capital charge for the roughly 81 affected properties (Lone Birch Trail / Maple Trail / Ridge Avenue area) was $17,097.38 as a lump sum, due April 15, 2026 — or automatic 20-year financing on the tax bill at an estimated 4.95% interest. That is down sharply from earlier estimates that ran $30,000 to $80,000 all-in. Private costs (grinder pump, permits, septic decommissioning) are extra and vary by property. Connection deadline is approximately end of 2028.
entries.keywords: lone birch maple trail ridge avenue hookup connection cost

entries.q: Who do I call about my water or wastewater bill?
entries.a: The township bills quarterly (meters read every 3 months). Billing questions: Township Financial Services at 705-484-5374, or the utilities clerk at alee@ramara.ca. Pay the same ways as property taxes — online banking, PaySimply (credit card, 2.5% fee), in person, dropbox, or pre-authorized payments. Late charge is 1.25% per month.
entries.keywords: bill payment quarterly meter invoice utilities

entries.q: Who do I call about water taste, quality, or seasonal shut-off?
entries.a: Municipal water systems are operated by the Ontario Clean Water Agency (OCWA). For water quality, taste, odour concerns, or to book seasonal shut-off/turn-on, call OCWA at 705-484-5600.
entries.keywords: ocwa taste smell discoloured shutoff turn on seasonal

entries.q: Water or sewer emergency — who do I call?
entries.a: Suspected water service or street leak during business hours: 705-484-5374 ext. 285. After hours, for any municipal road, water, or sewer emergency: 705-484-5374, press 9 (24/7 call centre).
entries.keywords: leak burst pipe sewage backup emergency after hours

entries.q: What is the Lagoon City levy on my tax bill?
entries.a: Lagoon City properties carry a separate special levy line on the tax bill (referenced in Bylaws 2023.33 and 2023.35). It funds Lagoon City-specific costs, including the private beaches/parks portion of the goose program. Tax bills there have up to four parts: general tax, water, wastewater, and the Lagoon City levy. For the current levy amount, contact the township.
entries.keywords: lagoon city special levy tax bill extra charge

entries.q: How do I report a pothole, plowing problem, or road issue?
entries.a: Report online through the township's Report a Concern portal (an email address is required — no anonymous online reports), or call Infrastructure Services at 705-484-5374 ext. 232 (infrastructure@ramara.ca). After-hours road emergencies: 705-484-5374, press 9.
entries.keywords: pothole snow plow grading dust washout report complaint

entries.q: Which roads are being worked on in 2026?
entries.a: Council approved the 2026 road program on May 11, 2026: Bridges 18 and 19, Ramara Road 46, Lakeshore Drive, Birch Road, Creighton Street, Concession Road 12, and Rama-Dalton Boundary Road, plus engineering. The township's Capital Projects page also lists ditching, hot-mix paving, and slurry-seal locations. The 2026 budget includes $4 million for road repairs and rehabilitation.
entries.keywords: construction paving schedule my road fixed when list

entries.q: How does the township decide which roads get fixed first?
entries.a: A 2025 Road Needs Study by Tatham Engineering (adopted in principle May 11, 2026) now guides priorities. The approach has shifted from 'worst first' to preserving roads still in fair/good shape, prioritizing higher-traffic roads, and using cost-saving methods. The study says Ramara should spend about $4.4M per year for 10 years; the 2026 budget has $4M. Full detail in our Roads brief.
entries.keywords: priority sequence order worst first asset management plan study

entries.q: How many roads does Ramara maintain?
entries.a: About 361 km of open roads: 183 km gravel and 178 km hard surface, maintained to Ontario's Minimum Maintenance Standards. County roads, provincial highways, private/unassumed roads, and Rama First Nation roads are not township-maintained.
entries.keywords: gravel paved kilometres network county highway who maintains

entries.q: When is my garbage day?
entries.a: Curbside garbage and organics are collected by the County of Simcoe. Garbage weeks alternate with recycling weeks; organics are weekly. Look up your schedule or sign up for reminders at simcoe.ca/wastereminder, or use the Simcoe County Collects app. Collection problems: 705-726-9300 or 1-866-893-9300.
entries.keywords: pickup day schedule trash organics green bin calendar

entries.q: Recycling changed in 2026 — who runs it now?
entries.a: As of January 1, 2026, recycling is managed by Circular Materials and collected by Emterra (no longer the County). For missed recycling pickup or cart repair, call Emterra at 1-888-597-1541 or email customercareont@emterra.ca. Garbage and organics are still County of Simcoe.
entries.keywords: blue box emterra circular materials missed recycling cart

entries.q: Where do I buy garbage bag tags?
entries.a: Bags beyond your cart need tags (max 5 tagged bags bi-weekly). Sold at: Brechin Foodland (2202 Hwy 12), Brechin One Stop (2692 Hwy 12), Mara Transfer Station, Ramara Fuels (5236 Hwy 12, Uptergrove), Rama General Store (5872 Rama Rd), and the Township office.
entries.keywords: extra bags tag sticker purchase overflow

entries.q: How do I get rid of large items (furniture, appliances)?
entries.a: The County of Simcoe runs bulky-item collections plus leaf/yard, Christmas tree, and battery collection weeks. Check current dates at simcoe.ca/waste. You can also take items to the Mara Waste Drop-off (see drop-off entry).
entries.keywords: couch mattress appliance fridge bulky furniture dispose

entries.q: Where is the dump / waste drop-off, and when is it open?
entries.a: Mara Waste Drop-off, 5200 County Road 169 — open Thursday to Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The County operates 8 drop-off facilities in total, including household hazardous waste depots.

links.label: All County drop-off locations and hours

entries.keywords: dump landfill transfer station hours hazardous paint electronics

entries.q: When are property taxes due in 2026?
entries.a: Interim bills: February 25 and April 27, 2026. Final bills: June 25 and September 25, 2026. Late penalty is 1.25% added on the 1st of each month and cannot be waived.
entries.keywords: due date deadline installment when pay property tax

entries.q: How can I pay my property taxes?
entries.a: Online or telephone banking (payee 'Ramara', 19-digit roll number starting 43-48); credit card through PaySimply (2.5% fee); cash, cheque, or debit at the township office; cheque in the dropbox by the main doors; by mail; or sign up for the pre-authorized payment plan. Paperless billing is also available.
entries.keywords: payment methods credit card online banking preauthorized

entries.q: Do I need a building permit, and how do I apply?
entries.a: Most construction needs a permit. Apply online through the Citywide portal (portal applications get priority over paper). Pools and fences do not need permits, though zoning and the fence bylaw still apply. Depending on location you may need LSRCA, MTO, or MNR approval first. Building Division: 705-484-5374 ext. 296, building@ramara.ca.
entries.keywords: renovation deck garage shed addition apply construction

entries.q: How do I book a building inspection?
entries.a: Give at least 48 hours notice. Book through the Citywide portal or call the inspection line: 705-484-5374 ext. 298.
entries.keywords: inspector framing footing final occupancy

entries.q: What do building permits cost?
entries.a: Fees are set in Schedule A of Bylaw 2023.22 (linked below). Pay by cash, cheque, or debit at the office; online payment on request.
entries.keywords: permit fee cost price schedule

entries.q: How do I file a bylaw complaint?
entries.a: Enforcement is complaint-driven and requires a written complaint (your identity is kept confidential). File online via the Report a Concern portal, by mail, or in person. Bylaw Enforcement: 705-484-5374 ext. 292, bylaw@ramara.ca. Criminal matters (vandalism, trespassing, dangerous driving) go to the OPP.
entries.keywords: noise complaint property standards parking enforcement neighbour

entries.q: What are the short-term rental rules in Ramara?
entries.a: Rentals under 28 days need an annual licence ($3,000) under Bylaw 2020.11 as amended. Maximum occupancy is 8 people. Administrative fines run $1,000 to $2,500. A map of licensed STRs is on the township's GIS. Penalty notices can be appealed to the Appeal Tribunal within 15 days.
entries.keywords: airbnb vrbo cottage rental licence rules occupancy

entries.q: The short-term rental next door is a problem — what do I do?
entries.a: First contact the rental's designated 'responsible person' (each licensed STR must have one). If unresolved, email bylaw@ramara.ca or file through the Report a Concern portal. For noise or disturbances that feel unsafe or criminal, call the OPP.
entries.keywords: party house noise airbnb complaint neighbour rental

entries.q: How do I get a dog licence, and what does it cost?
entries.a: Mandatory each year for dogs over 3 months. $20 + HST if bought on or before February 28; $50 + HST from March 1. Maximum 3 dogs per household. Buy online (4.5% card fee), by mail, or in person at the Township office or Ramara Centre.
entries.keywords: dog tag license renew pet registration

entries.q: I lost my dog / found a stray — who do I call?
entries.a: Animal services is run by Bylaw Enforcement: 705-484-5374 ext. 292 (business hours). After-hours canine emergencies: 705-623-7295. The township shelter is the Brechin Shelter, 3290 County Road 47 (lost, found, and adoptions). Dogs must be leashed on public property.
entries.keywords: stray lost found dog shelter pound loose bite ran away missing

entries.q: Do I need a burn permit?
entries.a: No — residential open-air burning is pre-approved, subject to conditions: no fire ban in effect, pile no bigger than 1 cubic metre, at least 5 m from structures and property lines, supervised at all times, wind under 25 km/h, organic materials only, and a way to put it out on hand. Check the posted daily Fire Danger Rating first. Bona fide farmers needing larger burns must call 705-484-5374 ext. 253 for approval.
entries.keywords: fire permit bonfire brush burn ban campfire rules

entries.q: How do I report an illegal or smoky burn?
entries.a: Business hours: 705-484-5374 ext. 253. After hours: 705-325-5201, option 4. If a fire is out of control or threatening property: call 911.
entries.keywords: smoke neighbour burning complaint illegal fire

entries.q: Who handles the geese problem?
entries.a: The township's Goose Management Program — created as a committee of council in November 2022, first piloted in Lagoon City in 2023, expanded to Lovely Day Park (Atherley) in 2024. For 2026 the township contracted Wildlife Management Group Inc. (1-888-557-5855), working under a federal wildlife permit: laser dissuaders, distress calls, dog and vehicle patrols, and nest/egg removal. Public-lands costs come from general taxes; the Lagoon City private beaches portion is funded by the Lagoon City levy. Questions: use the Report a Concern portal ('Goose Management Program Inquiry').
entries.keywords: geese goose poop droppings beach deterrent committee canada

entries.q: Can I get goose control on my private waterfront?
entries.a: Private landowners in the Lagoon City area can ask about participating in the goose program by emailing lc.goose.management@gmail.com. Elsewhere in the township, contact the Goose Management Program through the Report a Concern portal.
entries.keywords: private property beach geese landowner participate

entries.q: Where are the public boat launches?
entries.a: Eight township launches (use at your own risk, no docks): Bluebird Street (Lake St. John), Courtland Street (Lake Simcoe), Dalrymple Drive (Lake Dalrymple), Fern Resort Road (Lake Couchiching), Glenrest Drive (Lake Simcoe), Atherley Community Park / Lovely Day (Lake Simcoe), Poplar Lane (Lake Couchiching), and Suntrac Drive (Lake Simcoe — the only paved one).
entries.keywords: boat launch ramp lake simcoe couchiching dalrymple water access

entries.q: What parks and beaches does Ramara have?
entries.a: 13 township parks and 5 public Lake Simcoe beaches (unsupervised), plus Mara and McRae Point provincial parks. Playgrounds: Bluebird Park, Brechin Community Centre Park, Lovely Day Park (Atherley), and Lagoon City. There is an off-leash dog park at Brechin Community Park.
entries.keywords: beach playground picnic swimming park dog park

entries.q: How do I rent a community centre or hall?
entries.a: Ramara Centre (5482 Highway 12 South, Atherley — the main recreation hub): rentals via mmadden@ramara.ca. Longford Mills Community Centre: 705-326-3146. Udney Community Centre: 705-484-5482. Atherley Community Park hall: through Ramara Recreation.
entries.keywords: hall rental party event book community centre

entries.q: What are the library hours?
entries.a: Ramara Public Library (705-325-5776, info@ramarapubliclibrary.org). Ramara Centre Branch, 5482 Hwy 12 S: Tue–Thu 10–8, Fri 10–6, Sat 10–3, closed Sun/Mon. Brechin Branch (inside the Township office, 2297 Hwy 12): Thu 1–6, Sat 10–2.
entries.keywords: library books hours branch brechin atherley

entries.q: Is the sports dome happening?
entries.a: Not decided. As of June 2026 it is in a pre-feasibility stage: council approved commissioning a feasibility study contingent on grant funding (otherwise a $50K request in the 2027 budget). The only public cost estimate is up to $6.3M from a 2023 staff report. No dome has been approved, budgeted, or designed. Both sides of the debate are laid out in our Sports Dome brief.
entries.keywords: dome sports facility recreation soccer built status decision indoor

entries.q: Who is my councillor, and how do I reach them?
entries.a: Ramara has a 7-member council: Mayor Basil Clarke, Deputy Mayor Keith Bell (both elected at large), and one councillor in each of 5 wards — David Snutch (W1), Jennifer Fisher (W2), Dana Tuju (W3), Joe Gough (W4), Sherri Bell (W5). Full contacts and ward map on our Council page.
entries.keywords: ward councillor mayor deputy contact email phone who represents

entries.q: When does council meet, and can I watch?
entries.a: Council / Committee of the Whole meets twice monthly on Mondays at 9:30 a.m. (once only in July, August, and December) at the Administration Building, 2297 Highway 12, Brechin. Meetings are public and streamed on the township's YouTube channel and CivicWeb.
entries.keywords: council meeting schedule watch live stream when

entries.q: How do I speak at a council meeting?
entries.a: Two ways. Deputation (10 minutes, max 3 speakers): submit the request form with your materials by noon on the Monday before the meeting. Open Forum (1 minute, current agenda items only): register by 9 a.m. on meeting day. Clerk's office: 705-484-5374 ext. 235, clerks@ramara.ca.
entries.keywords: deputation delegate present speak address council voice

entries.q: Where do I find council agendas, minutes, and bylaws?
entries.a: Everything is on the township's CivicWeb portal. Agendas are posted the Friday before each meeting. You can subscribe by email to get them automatically.
entries.keywords: agenda minutes bylaw documents records civicweb

entries.q: How do I petition council?
entries.a: Petitions must use the township's template form, then be submitted through the online petition form or to the Clerk's office.
entries.keywords: petition signatures template submit

entries.q: When is the next municipal election?
entries.a: Monday, October 26, 2026. Nominations are open May 1 to August 21, 2026. Mayor Basil Clarke has announced he will not seek re-election. Candidate info and the official candidate list are on the township's elections page.
entries.keywords: election vote 2026 october candidates nomination run running for mayor council office

entries.q: How do I join a township committee?
entries.a: Ramara has 18+ boards, committees, and commissions — from the Climate Action Committee to the Trails Committee to the Youth Action Council. Citizen members are appointed; apply through the CivicWeb board application.
entries.keywords: volunteer committee board commission join apply

entries.q: Is the sports dome happening?
entries.a: Not decided. As of June 2026 it is in a pre-feasibility stage: council approved commissioning a feasibility study contingent on grant funding (otherwise a $50K request in the 2027 budget). The only public cost estimate is up to $6.3M from a 2023 staff report. No dome has been approved, budgeted, or designed. Both sides of the debate are laid out in our Sports Dome brief.

entries.q: Township office — address, phone, and hours?
entries.a: Township of Ramara Administration Building: 2297 Highway 12, PO Box 130, Brechin, ON L0K 1B0. Phone 705-484-5374, toll-free 1-800-663-4054, email ramara@ramara.ca. Open Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Payment dropbox to the right of the main doors (no cash).
entries.keywords: town hall office address hours phone contact municipal

entries.q: How do I report a problem to the township?
entries.a: Use the online Report a Concern portal — it routes roads, bylaw, animals, geese, and more to the right department. An email address is required; to report anonymously, call 705-484-5374 instead.
entries.keywords: complaint report issue problem portal concern

entries.q: After-hours emergency numbers
entries.a: Municipal road, water, or sewer emergency: 705-484-5374, press 9 (24/7). Canine control: 705-623-7295. Burning complaints: 705-325-5201, option 4. Fire or life-threatening emergency: 911. Police non-emergency: OPP.
entries.keywords: emergency after hours night weekend urgent
